hook: SCP-1055 opens by warning that the document itself is risky to read, and it means it. The procedures describe a carefully furnished home, a teddy bear that must never leave someone's arms, and staff who are deliberately kept misinformed. Pay close attention to who is being described in each paragraph.
whyItMatters: It is a good example of a Keter whose threat scales with attention, which turns the usual logic of an infohazard into a containment problem with no clean answer. The file ends with notes from three O5 members, a quick way to watch the Council split over ethics and cost. Its k-class-scenario tag makes clear that the stakes are far larger than the cozy procedures suggest.
thingsToNotice:
Notice the gap between the gentle tone of the care instructions and the severity of the description that follows. The meals, the books and the playroom are written with real warmth, and the article sets that warmth right beside catastrophic language. The whole arrangement rests on one person's kindness, and the document never lets you forget how fragile that is.

The closing O5 comments are worth reading as three distinct voices. One objects on moral grounds, one is coldly practical, and one treats the matter as a budget question; together they show the Foundation weighing a human being against a disaster. The file deliberately leaves that disagreement unresolved.

related.note: Another entity whose danger is set off simply by being perceived.
Another file where knowing about the subject is part of the danger.
